title: EnsembleElement
description: A single protective ensemble element (coat, pant, helmet, hood, gloves, boots, SCBA component). One record per physical item (or per lot, for lot-tracked items — see identifier.identifier_type). See 01-nfpa-1850-clause-mapping.md, NFPA 1851 Section 4.3, for the compliance rationale behind each field.

element_id.description: Compound identity key. Constructed as '{namespace}:{identifier.value}', where namespace = manufacturer_id when identifier.assigned_by = MANUFACTURER, or owning_organization_id when identifier.assigned_by = ORGANIZATION. This means uniqueness is guaranteed only within the namespace that assigned the identifier — see the identity note in the clause mapping doc.

manufacturer_id.description: NFPA 1851 4.3.3(3). Required regardless of identifier.identifier_type — manufacturer and model must be recorded even when the department assigns its own identifying number.

model.description: NFPA 1851 4.3.3(3): manufacturer and model name or design.

identifier.description: NFPA 1851 4.3.3(4): identification number, lot number, or serial number — plus PPE-REX's ORGANIZATION_ASSIGNED addition for items the manufacturer doesn't individually number.

assigned_by.description: Determines element_id's namespace and therefore the identifier's true uniqueness scope. ORGANIZATION means the value is only guaranteed unique within owning_organization_id's own numbering — not globally, and not guaranteed collision-free against another department's numbering if this element is ever transferred.

aliases.description: Optional, non-normative alternate identifiers — e.g., department asset tags like 'C104'. NFPA 1851 does not require these; they're included as a first-class field because the practice is common enough that leaving it to ad hoc vendor extensions would fragment it. PPE-REX does not parse or assign meaning to alias values (e.g., it does not infer that 'C104' means 'coat' or that it pairs with 'P104' — that convention lives in the department's own notes/practice, not in the standard).

scope_org_id.description: FK to Organization.org_id — the org within which this alias is meaningful/unique. Aliases are inherently local.

paired_element_ids.description: Optional, informal grouping — e.g., a coat and trousers issued together as a set, per local department convention (often signaled by matching asset-tag numbers like C104/P104). This is NOT the same as EnsembleConfiguration (NFPA 1851 4.3.4), which records a certified contaminant-protection grouping. paired_element_ids is a convenience/lookup field with no compliance meaning attached.

manufacture_date.description: NFPA 1851 4.3.3(5): month and year of manufacture only — intentionally not day-precision.

certification_refs.description: Applicable NFPA product standards this element is certified to (e.g., NFPA 1970).

owning_organization_id.description: FK to Organization.org_id — the department/agency that owns this element.

assigned_to_person_id.description: FK to Person.person_id — current wearer. Null for unassigned/spare gear, and expected to remain null between uses when rotation_program = true (NFPA 1851 4.3.5).

rotation_program.description: True if this element is tracked under NFPA 1851 4.3.5's rotating exchange program profile (not assigned to an individual member) rather than the 4.3.3 assigned-member profile. Changes which ServiceEvent types apply — see clause mapping doc.

retirement_date.description: NFPA 1851 4.3.3(10). Element-level summary; the authoritative record is the corresponding RETIREMENT ServiceEvent.

notes.description: Free-form notes at the element level. PPE-REX deliberately does not try to structure every possible department convention or edge case into controlled fields — unlike NFIRS's exhaustive code lists, this standard covers what NFPA 1851 requires as structured data and leaves department-specific detail to free text plus extensions, on the premise that modern search/AI-assisted extraction makes rigid taxonomies less necessary than they were when NFIRS was designed.

extensions.description: Vendor-specific fields, namespaced by reverse-DNS or registered prefix. Ignored by Core Conformant readers that don't recognize the namespace.
